title: Slow Cooker Braised Country-Style Ribs
cook: 6–7 hr on low, plus 25 min to finish

items: 3 lb bone-in country-style pork ribs (or beef short ribs)
¾ tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 large yellow onion, halved and sliced
1 cup low-sodium chicken broth (beef broth for short ribs)

steps: Pat the ribs completely dry. Mix the salt, pepper, smoked paprika and garlic powder, rub it all over the meat, and let it sit at room temperature up to 20 min while you heat the pan.

Heat the oil in a heavy 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the ribs in batches, about 3 min per side, until deeply browned. Don't crowd the pan. Move them to the slow cooker.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same skillet about 5 min, until softened. Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 1 min, until the paste darkens.
Pour in the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Whisk in the vinegar, Worcestershire, brown sugar and Dijon, bring to a simmer and pour over the ribs. Tuck in the bay leaf.
Cover and cook on low until fork-tender: 6–7 hr for pork, 8–9 hr for beef short ribs. The meat should offer no resistance to a fork but not fall completely apart.
Move the ribs to a foil-lined rimmed sheet pan. Strain the cooking liquid into a medium saucepan and skim off the fat.

Simmer the liquid over medium-high heat about 12 min, until reduced by about a third. Stir the cornstarch into the cold water, whisk it in and simmer 1–2 min, until glossy. Taste and adjust the salt or vinegar.
Heat the broiler. Brush the ribs generously with sauce and broil 3–5 min, watching closely, until the edges caramelize and blister. Serve with the rest of the sauce.
tips: Searing and the final broil are what keep this from tasting like generic slow-cooker meat. Don't skip them.
Keep the liquid low. The ribs should sit in it, not swim, or the sauce comes out thin.
For a barbecue version, swap half the broth for 1 cup of your favorite barbecue sauce and cut the brown sugar in half.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days in the sauce. Freezer up to 3 months. Reheat covered, in the sauce, in a 300°F oven until hot.
